raw_case_text:
A 14-year-old girl, offspring of a family who recently moved from Yemen to the United States, presented with symptoms of abdominal pain, polyuria and polydipsia, which had started a few weeks ago. The severity of the abdominal pain, described as dull, diffuse, and present for a long time, had increased in the past 2 days. The patient was reported to have had a protuberant abdomen since birth, which had shown no change in the recent past. She had frequent voidings that worsened over the last few weeks. She had a very good appetite. Ingestion of fluids was reported as adequate. The patient was born full term and had had no perinatal problems, but was developmentally delayed (talked and walked at age 4 years). At 8 years of age, she was diagnosed to have diabetes mellitus (DM) in Jordan by routine blood tests that showed a high blood sugar. Hypertension was diagnosed a few years later. The parents were told that the prognosis was poor. No treatment was offered for DM or hypertension. Breast development and pubic hair were noticed at age 9 years and axillary hair and body odor - at age 11 years. She had increased facial and body hair, but the age at which this was noticed was not clear. The patient had not yet started her menstrual periods. She had a history of poor dental hygiene and poor vision. The family history revealed a consanguineous relationship (distant cousins) between the father and mother who were otherwise healthy. The patient has three sisters and one brother who are all reported to have no medical problems. There is no family history of congenital or metabolic diseases. A review of the symptomatology is listed in Table 1, and the findings on physical examination are given in Table 2. Vital signs at presentation were: pulse: 98/min, blood pressure: 144/84 mmHg, respiration: 20 /min, afebrile. She weighed 40.3 kg (5th percentile for age, -1.7 SD) and her height was 144 cm (under the 3rd percentile, -2.25 SDS), her body mass index(BMI) was 19.4 kg /m2 (0.00 SD). The pertinent features were: absence of subcutaneous fat in the extremities, face, trunk and hands; prominent muscles; looking much older than her stated age; dysmorphic features; developmental delay; hepatosplenomegaly; poor vision; enophthalmus; and arthropathy. There was no evidence of retinopathy. Laboratory data are listed in Table 3. Her serum glucose was 393 mg/dL and there was no metabolic acidosis. Given the history of fever and hepatosplenomegaly, screening for human immunodeficiency virus, Hepatitis A, B, C, and tuberculin test were done, and were all negative. Imaging studies demonstrated striking organomegaly involving the liver, spleen, and kidneys. Stool impaction was evident on X-ray. Ultrasound of the abdomen showed hepatomegaly, enlargement of the main portal vein, numerous splenic varices, and splenomegaly indicating a mild degree of portal hypertension. Radiograms showed mottled bones. Echocardiogram revealed aortic insufficiency and left ventricular hypertrophy. Chromosomal analysis specifically for mutation of 11q13 and 9q34 is not yet completed.
The clinical features and laboratory data of this patient suggested a diagnosis of congenital lipodystrophy, and more specifically of BSCL2. She was started on an insulin regimen of 1 unit/kg/day and increased up to 6 units/kg/day (300 units daily). Her present insulin regimen includes glargine (100 units) at bedtime and aspart (40-60 units) before each meal. Given the risks of liver toxicity associated with metformin, metformin was started at 250 mg once a day and gradually increased to 500 mg twice a day. Liver function tests were monitored every 6 weeks. Even with combined insulin and metformin therapy, her blood sugar has remained in the 200-500mg/dL range. Her hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), which was 12.2% at diagnosis, had improved to 10.6% over a 6-month period. She is encouraged to do more physical activity. She was also started on ergocalciferol and calcium for vitamin D deficiency. The carious teeth were extracted. For persistent proteinuria and nephromegaly, a kidney biopsy was done that showed IgA nephropathy. She was placed on angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor for persistent proteinuria and hypertension. Her blood pressure has normalized on antihypertensive medication. Portal hypertension has been monitored closely as these patients are at risk for esophageal varices.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 14-year-old girl who recently emigrated from Yemen to the United States presented with a several-week history of worsening polyuria, polydipsia, and diffuse abdominal pain that intensified over the preceding 2 days.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient had a lifelong protuberant abdomen and chronic dull abdominal pain that acutely worsened 2 days prior to presentation, accompanied by several weeks of worsening polyuria and polydipsia despite a voracious appetite and adequate fluid intake.
subjective.past_medical_history: Born full-term without perinatal complications; global developmental delay (walked and talked at age 4 years); untreated diabetes mellitus diagnosed in Jordan at age 8 years and untreated hypertension diagnosed several years later; premature adrenarche/thelarche (breast and pubic hair at age 9, axillary hair at age 11), hirsutism, primary amenorrhea at age 14, poor vision, and severe dental caries. Born to consanguineous parents (distant cousins) with four healthy siblings.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for abdominal pain, abdominal distension, polyuria, polydipsia, polyphagia, hirsutism, primary amenorrhea, poor vision, and joint stiffness/arthropathy.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs: pulse 98/min, blood pressure 144/84 mmHg, respiratory rate 20/min, afebrile; weight 40.3 kg (5th percentile, -1.7 SD), height 144 cm (<3rd percentile, -2.25 SD), and BMI 19.4 kg/m2 (0.00 SD). Physical findings included generalized absence of subcutaneous adipose tissue across the face, trunk, limbs, and hands, prominent muscular hypertrophy, acromegaloid/progeroid facial appearance, dysmorphic features, enophthalmos, developmental delay, massive hepatosplenomegaly, arthropathy, poor visual acuity without diabetic retinopathy, and extensive dental caries.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission serum glucose was 393 mg/dL without ketoacidosis; baseline HbA1c was 12.2% (improving to 10.6% at 6 months); vitamin D deficiency and persistent proteinuria were present. Screening tests for HIV, Hepatitis A, B, and C, and tuberculin skin test were all negative. Abdominal X-ray showed fecal impaction and skeletal radiographs showed mottled bone density; abdominal ultrasound demonstrated hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, dilated main portal vein, and splenic varices consistent with mild portal hypertension.
objective.advanced_workup: Transthoracic echocardiogram demonstrated aortic insufficiency and left ventricular hypertrophy. Percutaneous renal biopsy performed for persistent proteinuria and nephromegaly confirmed IgA nephropathy. Genetic testing for 11q13 (BSCL2/seipin) and 9q34 (AGPAT2) mutations was initiated.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Berardinelli-Seip congenital generalized lipodystrophy type 2 (BSCL2, HIV-negative) complicated by severe insulin-resistant diabetes mellitus (baseline glucose 393 mg/dL, HbA1c 12.2%), arterial hypertension, left ventricular hypertrophy, aortic insufficiency, hepatosplenomegaly with mild portal hypertension, vitamin D deficiency, and biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy. Management included high-dose basal-bolus insulin therapy titrated up to 6 units/kg/day (300 units/day: insulin glargine 100 units nightly plus pre-meal insulin aspart 40–60 units), metformin titrated to 500 mg twice daily with 6-weekly LFT monitoring (reducing HbA1c to 10.6% at 6 months), ACE inhibitor therapy (normalizing blood pressure and treating IgA nephropathy/proteinuria), ergocalciferol and calcium supplementation, dental extractions, and ongoing surveillance for portal hypertension.
